title: Fatima, 1917
hook: three shepherd children and a call to prayer and penance

segments.voice: Yesterday, Charles de Foucauld, the soldier who became a universal brother among the Tuareg. Your line was brother to everyone. Today, shepherd children, and a jail cell.

A town official in Portugal loads some children into his carriage. They are shepherds from the hamlet of Aljustrel, near Fatima: Lucia and her cousins Francisco and Jacinta. For months they have said that a lady from heaven appears to them on the thirteenth of each month, and crowds now follow them to the field. The official is not a believer, and his government is suspicious of the Church. He wants the crowds gone and the children's secret out. Instead of taking them to the field, he takes them to his town and locks them up.
screen: `A CARRIAGE, A TOWN OFFICIAL.` → `CROWDS IN A FIELD.` → `CHILDREN LOCKED UP.`

segments.voice: Stay with those few days. First, the message. The children said the lady asked them to pray the rosary every day for peace and the end of the war, and to do penance, small sacrifices offered for others. Europe was at war, and Portuguese soldiers were in it. Second, the pressure. In Lucia's later memoirs, the official questioned them, and when they refused to tell what the lady had confided, he threatened them with death. They were frightened. They still wouldn't tell. Third, the cell. Lucia recalled that they were put in a room with the town's prisoners. Jacinta was crying for her mother. Then the children knelt and began the rosary, and some of the prisoners knelt and prayed with them: grown men in a jail, following children through the Hail Mary. Fourth, the outcome. The children were sent home, and they said the lady came again a few days later, in a different spot. In the end the Church judged the appearances worthy of belief; Catholics are free to accept them or not, since the Church calls such events private revelations. At the center is a prayer older than Fatima, the angel's words in Luke's Gospel, in the Douay-Rheims, "Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women." This week ran through a freed slave, an heiress, an immigrant, a little book, children at the altar, a desert brother, and now children praying in a jail.
screen: `THE ROSARY, FOR PEACE.` · `THREATENED, AND SILENT.` · `PRISONERS KNEEL WITH CHILDREN.` · `WORTHY OF BELIEF, NOT REQUIRED.` · then, large: `HAIL, FULL OF GRACE.`

segments.voice: A whole rosary won't fit here, so take a small piece of it. Bring to mind one place at war right now; if you pray, say the Hail Mary slowly, once or a few times, for the people there, on beads or on your fingers. If you don't, hold that place in silence and wish its people safety and an end to the fighting.
Fatima. A village in Portugal where, the children said, a lady asked for the rosary, penance, and prayer for peace.
Your line: pray for peace. The children prayed it in a frightening place. That's a week: day nine hundred three.

howItsDone: Catholics keep Our Lady of Fatima on 13 May; pilgrims go to the shrine at Fatima, and in parishes people pray the rosary together, often adding a prayer for peace.

options: No. The Church judged them worthy of belief, but Catholics are free to accept them or not.
Yes. Once the Church approves a vision, every Catholic must believe it like the Creed.
No. The Church has never said anything about Fatima, either for it or against it.

Year-two day 668 covered the Fatima story overall, the sun, and private revelation as its myth; this day takes the August jailing at Ourém as its angle to avoid repetition.

Jailing details (taken by the administrator of Ourém, Artur de Oliveira Santos; threatened with death, tradition says by boiling oil; put with prisoners; rosary prayed; prisoners joining; Jacinta crying for her mother) follow Lucia's memoirs; confirm.
'His government is suspicious of the Church' (the anticlerical First Republic): confirm wording.
Later appearance 'a few days later, in a different spot' refers to Valinhos (19 August); confirm.
Claims rule: no ages, no crowd size, and no approval year given. 'Portuguese soldiers were in it' (Portugal in the First World War): confirm.
CCC 67 on private revelation: confirm citation.
